sources_considered.why: Provides directly measured factual precision for contemporary language models.
Reports causal reasoning successes alongside unpredictable failures, directly relevant to the proposed inference.
A relevant additional limitation, but it does not identify hallucinations as evidence of an absence of all common-sense reasoning.

evidence_items.explanation: The biography evaluation supports the premise that contemporary models frequently produced unsupported factual statements. It does not measure all forms of hallucination, individual-error unpredictability, or absence of common sense.

The authors report successes in causal discovery and counterfactual tasks while also reporting unpredictable failure modes. Their results caution against treating failures as sufficient proof of an absence of reasoning, but benchmark success does not establish robust general common sense.

unresolved_gaps: No cited study establishes the causal or diagnostic link from hallucinations to an absence of common sense.
The evidence does not supply a general threshold for true common sense.
Measured factual precision does not establish that errors are unpredictable in the sense Marcus intended.
